dedupe_keys.name: usgs data for assessment of mineral commodity supply risk 2018 critical minerals list inputs

description: This U.S. Geological Survey data release holds the data behind Figure 2 of Open-File Report 2021-1045, the methodology and technical input for the 2021 review of the US critical minerals list: disruption potential, economic vulnerability, trade exposure and overall supply risk scores for mineral commodities in 2018. The ScienceBase and DataCite pages say some indicator scores are rounded to avoid disclosing company proprietary data. It was published on 24 April 2025 by Nedal Nassar and Steven Fortier as one CSV of about 9 KB with a PNG figure and XML metadata, downloadable and free under CC0 1.0. Coverage is the US economy's exposure to global supply, one row per commodity. Caveats: it is one year, scores are rounded, and the full method is in the report, not on the page read. For simulation it gives a ready ranking of which mineral inputs carry the highest disruption and trade risk, useful to choose commodities for supply shock scenarios and to weight critical inputs in manufacturing and energy supply chain models. Related catalogue records include the USGS world minerals outlook to 2029, the USGS Critical mineral deposits of the United States and the EV battery cathode material flows.
